title: Solving Quadratic Trigonometric Equations
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Solve the trigonometric equation 2*cos^2(x) - cos(x) - 1 = 0 for all solutions in the interval [0, 2*pi).

steps.title: Treat as a Quadratic in cos(x)
steps.explanation: Substitute u = cos(x) to recognize the equation as a standard quadratic trinomial.
steps.why: Algebraic substitution reveals the underlying polynomial structure of trigonometric equations.

steps.title: Factor the Quadratic
steps.explanation: Factoring gives two distinct linear factors: 2*cos(x) + 1 = 0 or cos(x) - 1 = 0.
steps.why: The Zero Product Property requires at least one factor to vanish.

steps.title: Solve Each Branch on [0, 2*pi)
steps.explanation: On the interval [0, 2*pi), cos(x) = 1 only at x = 0. Cosine equals -1/2 in Quadrants II and III at the reference angle pi/3, yielding x = pi - pi/3 = 2*pi/3 and x = pi + pi/3 = 4*pi/3.
steps.why: Unit circle symmetry yields two solutions for negative cosine in Quadrants II and III.
